utterances.text: Well, let's examine paragraph IX: "The chief of the Main Staff shall head the Main Staff." Okay? "The chief of the Main Staff shall be responsible to the head of the department," and then it specifies for what sort of tasks, "proposing and implementing measures, for all administrative tasks, and issues relating the budget and material supplies, and the consumption of general organisation of civilian life, as well as wartime organisation of the armed forces." The next paragraph says: "The chief of the Main Staff shall be directly responsible to the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, for all issues relating to the Supreme Command unit organisation, strategic and operative plans, and the use of the armed forces in times of war and peace." So I think this is beginning to establish the chain of command from the president through the chief of the Main Staff who heads the Main Staff. It then goes on to say: "The chief of the Main Staff shall exercise superior authority over the command of the Croatian Defence Council within the scope of general and specific powers vested in him." "Brigade commanders shall be subordinate and responsible to the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna as the commander-in-chief of the armed forces." So I think that is the -- that appears to me to be the same chain of command that I've referred to, from president through the chief of the Main Staff down to the subordinate formations.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. That was my question, in fact. So you agree that the conclusions that you drew in your report were more or less identical to the contents of this document which you had not previously seen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW PRINGLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's a fair statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please, could you tell me the following: Have you ever seen a document about when and where military cabinet was established? I'm referring to 25 -- paragraph 25, of your report. Have you ever seen such a document?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW PRINGLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which part of paragraph 25 are you referring me to?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Practically, the penultimate line. Reference is made to the military cabinet -- war cabinet appointed by the Supreme Commander. It's at the end of 25?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW PRINGLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I've referenced that as footnote 5, which appears to be Exhibit 00289.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: No, sir. It's -- 289 is a decree on armed forces. I'm just asking you whether you can remember this. If not, just say so. But have you ever seen a document on the basis of which a war cabinet was established, and when was such a cabinet established? 289 is a decree on the armed forces of the HZ HB, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW PRINGLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've referenced the decree on the armed forces of Herceg-Bosna as footnote 4, and I have therefore seen it. In fact, I go on to say, in effect, this enshrines political control over the military as one would expect.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And that is why I'm putting this question to you. You referred to the decree on the armed forces, which prescribes for the establishment of a war cabinet. But now I'm asking you whether you ever saw a single document about whether a war cabinet had been established and when? That's all I'm asking you. Did you ever see such a document?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW PRINGLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I haven't referenced it or mentioned it, then I assume I did not, but that's -- I'm talking about how it was set up here. Whether it was actually set up, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. That's your answer. Have you seen a document establishing a defence council? You refer to such a defence council in paragraph 26, the penultimate sentence of your report.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW PRINGLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I assume I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'll put the question to you again.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW PRINGLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't understand your answer. You assume what, that you saw a decision on establishing the defence council? I'd just like to remind you that that is not stated anywhere in the footnotes.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW PRINGLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've written here: "The military and political aspects of defence would be integrated in the defence council and the defence department. "The Main Staff would be responsible for performing the stipulated tasks in accordance with defence policy." I assume I have written that -- I assume I have written that based on the documents that I have seen. Are you telling me it's wrong?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I can't tell you that it's wrong. But if you saw any such thing, my question would be where. That sentence is very important, so I'm asking you whether you have ever seen a document, on the basis of which military and political aspects of defence were adopted by the defence council and defence department. Have you ever seen such a document? This is an assumption, and you haven't provided a basis for it. I'm asking you whether this is just your assumption, or did you ever have the opportunity to examine some document that you haven't referred to in your report? I'm referring to the sentence we have just read out. So are you making an assumption, or have you seen the basis for such a claim?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW PRINGLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the Defence has been provided with a list of the documents with which I was furnished.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I received them, and I read through them very carefully, and I came to the conclusion that there wasn't a single piece of evidence, and you didn't refer to any such evidence in your footnotes either. There wasn't a single piece of evidence that would demonstrate the origin or the basis for this sentence. We all have your report, and we'll judge it ourselves. But can you remember whether this is an assumption or can you refer whether this is just an assumption or were you shown a document that force the basis for this conclusion? Let's be clear about this. I am a Defence lawyer, and I have to verify the credibility of your report. Your report is here, and it's very important for us to know whether you are making an assumption here or whether what you claim here is based on some regulations or on some document that you may have had the opportunity to examine?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW PRINGLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have written will have been based on the documents that I read, and you have a list of the documents I was furnished with.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Your answer is that you cannot now remember whether you ever saw a document of any kind or whether this sentence that we see here is a conclusion of a personal kind that you came to?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW PRINGLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will recall that I wrote my report in March 2006. I was furnished with a long list of documents. I read and studied those documents. I wrote my report. It's now November 2007. I cannot remember in detail which document I -- I read to make that statement. It doesn't mean I did; doesn't mean I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, I'm really examining you in your capacity as an expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. I am a bit lost. I find this reference to the defence council in paragraph 25 and 26, and there is a reference to exhibit 00289, Article 9. I looked that up and there it says: "The Croatian Defence Council shall," and then a lot of tasks are named. You seemed to have said that there was no such thing as a defence council, or that it didn't figure anywhere. I must have misunderstood you somehow.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The difference is between what is in the rules and what actually took place. I'm just trying to ask the witness a question. I know that it's contained in the rules on the military forces, but I'm asking the witness whether this sentence is based on the rules and regulations one can consult or whether he saw a document which is the basis for establishing this defence council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise for interrupting, Your Honour. Judge Trechsel just made part of the point that I wanted to make. I think that the report, read on its face, says quite clearly in paragraph 25, where at that point, he says a range of powers would normally be vested in some form of defence council. He's stating, in that particular context, a concept in that particular instance. He does go on to talk, to make other references to Defence council and then later to war cabinet. But as Judge Trechsel just pointed out, those concepts can, in fact, be found in P 00289. And with great respect to my friend Ms. Nozica, there are two separate questions that are being mixed together here. One is she keeps asking the witness: Did you see a document to that effect? Well, Exhibit P 00289. Then, she says: But I am asking him, whatever the paper says, that it really exists in practice. But those are two completely separate questions that are being mixed to the, I'm afraid. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there's a translation error that's quite clear, and what Judge Trechsel said makes this clear. We're talking about a military council here. The translation is defence council. It should be military council, because the regulations provide for a military council. That's why there is a misunderstanding, because the Defence asks whether he saw a document showing that such a defence council was established. So there's, obviously, a translation error here, which makes one thing of a different body. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to thank Mr. Prlic, but here this is one thing that is very important. The expert witness has provided his opinion on the relationship between the political aspects, the Supreme Command, the defence department of the Main Staff. This was on the basis of some documents he was provided with. He provided his assessment of the situation in 25 and 26 -- in paragraphs 25 and 26, and paragraph 79 of his report. He provided the assessment of those relationships. These relationships could have existed on paper, but they could also have been implemented, and this is a different matter. So I'm now asking the witness this question. It's true that this is what it says in the decree on the armed forces, but I'm now asking him whether he has drawn his conclusion on the basis of the decree or on the basis that such a situation was, in fact, brought about. That was the purpose of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you, that clarifies.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That seems very logical to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once you answer, then we'll have to stop here because we're coming to the end of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. My report is written and referenced on the basis of the decree referenced as 00289, from which I drew the information. You may say I made the assumption that the decree, having been written, it was executed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, General, sir. Tomorrow, Mrs. Nozica, your questioning will continue tomorrow, and we'll see how much time you have left.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me now ask the usher to please take the witness back. General, you will be returning here tomorrow for the hearing in afternoon. Let's go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, before we move into private session, I'll just need a few seconds. Before listening to the examination-in-chief of this military expert, I believe that the Judges understood the reasons for the Petkovic Defence for requesting additional time for cross-examination, because on the basis of the prepared documents, it was quite clear that many orders would be discussed, orders signed by my client, General Petkovic. Therefore, I would now like to orally repeat my request to be granted additional time, and I would appreciate it if you could reconsider your decision on allow the Petkovic Defence to have more than an hour for cross-examination. In the transcript, it is Vesna Alaburic on behalf of General Petkovic, not Ms. Nozica. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll wait for -- I'll wait for the signal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 7th day of November, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.
